rejected.title: The remainder and factor theorems
card: Remainder theorem
When P(x) is divided by (x − a), the remainder is P(a). To find it, substitute x = a. No long division is needed.
Factor theorem
If P(a) = 0, then (x − a) is a factor of P(x). If P(a) is not 0, then (x − a) is not a factor.
Rational root theorem
Take P(x) with whole number coefficients. Any rational root p/q in lowest terms has p dividing the constant term and q dividing the leading coefficient.
Example
Let P(x) = x³ − 2x² − 5x + 6. P(1) = 1 − 2 − 5 + 6 = 0, so (x − 1) is a factor. P(2) = 8 − 8 − 10 + 6 = −4, so dividing by (x − 2) leaves remainder −4.
rejected.remember: Substitute a into P(x): the answer is the remainder, and 0 means (x − a) is a factor.

a.q: What is the remainder when P(x) = x³ + 2x − 5 is divided by (x − 2)?
a.why: The remainder is P(2) = 8 + 4 − 5 = 7. The option −17 comes from substituting x = −2, giving −8 − 4 − 5 = −17, but the divisor (x − 2) means x = 2.
a.clue: Substitute the value that makes x − 2 equal zero.

b.q: For which value of k is (x + 3) a factor of P(x) = x³ + kx² − 4x − 12?
b.why: (x + 3) is a factor when P(−3) = 0. P(−3) = −27 + 9k + 12 − 12 = 9k − 27, so k = 3. Using x = 3 instead gives 27 + 9k − 12 − 12 = 9k + 3, which gives k = −1/3, so it is not an option.
b.clue: Set P(−3) = 0 and solve for k.
